I have consistently maintained my reporting and tracking sheet by updating daily call activities, monitoring data accuracy, and ensuring that all lead stages are correctly recorded based on discussions with merchants.

For merchants who were marked as "Not Interested," I proactively reconnected with them to better understand the reasons behind their decision to discontinue using Razorpay and their reluctance to return. During these conversations, I also explored whether there were any concerns or challenges that we could address to improve their overall experience with Razorpay.

In cases where merchants remained uninterested and did not provide a specific reason for their decision, I escalated those leads to Gauri, who manages churn revival, for a second level of follow-up. This ensured that every lead was validated appropriately and that all fields in my tracking sheet were updated accurately, without any incorrect or incomplete inputs.

text:
A significant number of merchants in my lead sheet consistently fell under the "Did Not Pick" (DNP) or "Did Not Answer" category. As part of my regular follow-up process, I shared WhatsApp messages with these merchants after unsuccessful call attempts. However, the response rate through WhatsApp remained minimal.

To improve merchant engagement, I proposed and initiated an automated email campaign targeting these DNP merchants. The objective was to evaluate whether structured email follow-ups could generate responses from merchants who were unresponsive through calls and WhatsApp. This campaign was my initiative, and Vamsee supported me in implementing it successfully.

Within a week of launching the campaign, we began receiving email responses from merchants who had previously been unreachable through other communication channels. The early results indicate that the campaign has been effective in increasing merchant engagement and has introduced an additional outreach channel that complements our existing follow-up process.
